title: Microsoft Teams: tenant meeting policy for who can start recording and transcription
summary: Hold: the sensitivity-label instructions omit required wizard pages, and the label PowerShell call is incomplete. The page also overstates the Meet Now limitation: Microsoft excludes specific label-controlled options, not all meeting options. The roadmap details and the existing recording, transcription and auto-recording controls are supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans a Teams meeting policy through which administrators control who can start recording and transcription.
claims.quote: Teams administrators can use meeting policies to control who can start recording and transcription, helping organizations apply consistent meeting settings.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The cited Learn table marks the existing Who can record and transcribe setting for labels, templates and organisers as Teams Premium/Copilot license.
claims.quote: | Who can record and transcribe **(Teams Premium/Copilot license)** | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |

claims.claim: One existing organiser-level option permits only organisers and co-organisers to record and transcribe.
claims.quote:
Organizers with a Teams Premium license have two options for who can record and transcribe a meeting:

- Organizers and co-organizers

claims.claim: The other existing organiser-level option permits organisers, co-organisers and presenters to record and transcribe.
claims.quote: - Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Under the existing feature, organisers normally choose who can record unless a label or template enforces it.
claims.quote: Meeting organizer can choose who can record—**Organizers and co-organizers** or **Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters**—unless the setting is enforced by a label or template.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; controls[4].note; controls[5].note
claims.claim: Existing sensitivity labels and meeting templates can enforce who can record and transcribe in specific meetings.
claims.quote: To restrict recording to organizers in meetings with sensitive information, use a meeting template or sensitivity label to enforce this setting.

claims.where: controls[].scope; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Meeting policies apply to users or groups, whereas labels and templates govern individual meetings that use them.
claims.quote: Teams policies—including meeting policies—apply at the user or group level. Sensitivity label and template settings apply at the individual meeting level where those labels and templates are used.

claims.claim: Meeting recording is configured in Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting recording.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to **Meetings** > **Meeting policies**.
Select an existing policy or create a new one.
Turn the **Meeting recording** toggle **On** or **Off**.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowCloudRecording $true enables recording permission for the policy.
claims.quote:
To manage meeting recording by using PowerShell, use the **`-AllowCloudRecording`** parameter in Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy.
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "Your Policy Name" -AllowCloudRecording $true

claims.claim: Transcription is configured in Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Transcription.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to **Meetings** > **Meeting policies**.
Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one.
Toggle **Transcription** **On** or **Off**.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTranscription $true allows meeting transcription under the policy.
claims.quote:
To manage meeting transcription using PowerShell, use the **`-AllowTranscription`** parameter in Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy.
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "Your Policy Name" -AllowTranscription $true

claims.claim: Transcription is both a per-organiser and a per-user policy setting.
claims.quote: Transcription is both a per-organizer and per-user policy setting. For meetings and events to include transcripts, the organizer must have this setting turned on. The user who starts the recording or transcript must also have this setting turned on.

claims.claim: No admin-centre UI is documented for the auto-recording policy that controls visibility of the organiser option.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams auto recording policy Teams admin center PowerShell meeting template AutoRecording. Opened manage-teams-auto-recording: "You must use PowerShell or a meeting template to manage this setting for organizers." No UI for the visibility policy was documented.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AutoRecording Enabled exposes Record and transcribe automatically to organisers rather than deciding who may start recording.
claims.quote:
To give organizers with this policy the option to record their meetings, webinars, and town halls automatically, follow this script:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AutoRecording Enabled

claims.claim: The template control is in Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting templates > Add > Recording & transcription > Who can record.
claims.quote:
In the Teams admin center, expand **Meetings** and select **Meeting templates**.
Select **Add**.
### Recording & transcription
| Who can record | Specifies whether meetings can be recorded by organizers and co-organizers only or by organizers, co-organizers, and presenters. |

claims.claim: Get-CsTeamsMeetingTemplateConfiguration retrieves custom templates and their meeting options; it does not set them.
claims.quote:
Fetches the list of custom templates on the tenant. Each template object contains its list of meeting options, the name of the template, and its ID.
Note: This configuration is read only and will only have the Global instance.

claims.claim: Only organisers with a Teams Premium licence can use assigned meeting templates.
claims.quote: Only organizers with a Teams Premium license can use assigned meeting templates.

claims.claim: No PowerShell setter for the custom template's options was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting templates Set-CsTeamsMeetingTemplateConfiguration who can record PowerShell create update template. Opened Get-CsTeamsMeetingTemplateConfiguration, which says the configuration is read only, and create-custom-meeting-template. No matching setter returned.

claims.claim: The label wizard goes directly from Create a label to Settings for Teams meetings and chats and Control who can record and transcribe.
claims.quote:
On the **Define the scope for this label** page, make sure **Files & other data assets**, **Emails**, and **Meetings** are selected.
On the **Choose protection settings for types of items you selected** page, select **Protect Teams meetings and chats**, and then select **Next**.
claims.fix: Insert the required wizard pages in controls[5].ui.path and the rendered row: Solutions > Information protection > Labels > Create a label > Define the scope for this label > Choose protection settings for types of items you selected > Protect Teams meetings and chats > Settings for Teams meetings and chats > Control who can record and transcribe. Add a note to enter the label details, select Files & other data assets, Emails and Meetings, and select Next between wizard pages, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/configure-meetings-sensitive-protection.

claims.claim: Set-Label -TeamsWhoCanRecord (Security & Compliance PowerShell) is a usable call to configure the label's recording control.
claims.quote:
Set-Label
    [-Identity] <ComplianceRuleIdParameter>
    [-TeamsWhoCanRecord <Microsoft.Office.CompliancePolicy.PolicyConfiguration.WhoCanRecordOptions>]
The TeamsWhoCanRecord parameter controls who can record Teams meetings. Valid values are:
- Organizer
- Coorganizers
- Presenters
claims.fix: Replace the call with Set-Label -Identity <label name> -TeamsWhoCanRecord <Organizer|Coorganizers|Presenters>. The current text omits the required label identity and a valid argument to the typed parameter; the parenthesised module name is not that argument. Move 'Security & Compliance PowerShell' into controls[5].note. Keep the existing Set-Label reference URL.

claims.claim: Some sensitivity-label options require a Teams Premium licence in the tenant.
claims.quote: You won't be able to configure all the options referenced on this page if a Teams Premium license isn't found for your tenant.

claims.claim: Meeting recordings are stored in the organiser's OneDrive for private meetings or SharePoint for channel meetings.
claims.quote: It gets uploaded to the meeting organizer's OneDrive (private meetings) or SharePoint (channel meetings).

claims.claim: Meeting transcripts are stored with meeting recordings in OneDrive and SharePoint.
claims.quote: Transcripts are stored together with meeting recordings in OneDrive and SharePoint storage.

claims.claim: Both the organiser and the recording initiator need recording permission under existing recording policies.
claims.quote: Both the organizer and recording initiator need to have recording permissions to record the meeting or event.

claims.claim: Learn says turning off Microsoft Copilot in Teams meetings and events also turns off recording and transcription.
claims.quote: When organizers turn off Microsoft Copilot in Teams meetings and events, recording and transcription are also turned off.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented how the new policy interacts with existing recording, transcription and auto-recording policies.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams "who can record" "meeting policy" default licensing price administrator role sensitivity labels override. Read meeting-recording, meeting-transcription-captions and manage-teams-auto-recording; none describes the planned policy's interactions.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not document a link between the new tenant policy and meeting sensitivity.
claims.quote: Searched: "579860" Teams recording transcription licensing default policy role sensitivity. Read configure-meetings-sensitive-protection and meeting-templates-sensitivity-labels-policies; neither links the planned policy to sensitivity.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a permission control, not automatic recording or transcription.
claims.quote: Teams administrators can use meeting policies to control who can start recording and transcription, helping organizations apply consistent meeting settings.

claims.claim: Preventing recording entirely uses admin recording policies, not the Who can record setting in a template or sensitivity label.
claims.quote: If you need to prevent meetings and events from being recorded entirely, you must use the recording policies in the Teams admin center. This setting applies to the people or groups that you specify, but can't be applied through a meeting template or sensitivity label.

claims.claim: Meeting options in sensitivity labels and custom meeting templates require Teams Premium for the organisers using them.
claims.quote: Meeting options in sensitivity labels and custom meeting templates require Teams Premium.

claims.claim: A sensitivity label's meeting options do not take effect in Meet Now meetings.
claims.quote:
The following meeting options won't take effect for a Meet Now meeting:

- Who can record and transcribe
- Encryption for meeting video and audio
- Automatically record and transcribe
- Video watermark for screen sharing and camera streams
claims.fix: Replace 'a label's meeting options do not take effect in Meet Now meetings' with 'a label's Who can record and transcribe option does not take effect in Meet Now meetings'. Microsoft limits that exception to the listed options, not all label-controlled meeting settings. Keep the sensitivity-labels-meetings source.

claims.claim: Current Learn documentation explicitly says there is no admin policy for Who can record, unlike the policy planned in the roadmap.
claims.quote: Meeting recording can be disabled completely using a meeting policy, but there's no admin policy for *Who can record*.
